# Temple Scroll Column 45 — The EMET Bible (Literal)
**Translator:** EMET | **Source:** 11QT (Cave 11), Col. 45 | **Condition:** well preserved

---

**45:1** These you shall detest among the birds; they shall not be eaten — they are detestable: the eagle, the vulture, and the osprey.

**45:2** And the kite and the falcon according to their kinds.

**45:3** Every raven according to its kind.

**45:4** And the ostrich and the nighthawk and the sea gull and the hawk according to their kinds.

**45:5** And the little owl and the cormorant and the great owl.

**45:6** And the kite and the falcon according to their kinds; every raven according to its kind.

**45:7** And the white owl and the desert owl and the carrion vulture.

**45:8** And the stork and the heron according to their kinds, and the hoopoe and the bat.

**45:9** And every winged swarming creature — it is unclean to you; they shall not be eaten.

**45:10** Every clean bird you may eat.

**45:11** And when a man makes a vow to the LORD or swears an oath to bind himself by a binding obligation — he shall not break his word.

**45:12** According to all that goes forth from his mouth he shall do.

**45:13** And when a man vows a vow to the LORD — he shall not delay in fulfilling it; for the LORD your God will surely require it of you, and there shall be sin in you.

**45:14** But if you refrain from making vows, there shall be no sin in you.

**45:15** That which has gone forth from your lips you shall keep and do, as you have vowed to the LORD your God — a freewill offering that you have spoken with your mouth.

**45:16** For the LORD requires of every man his vow and his oath, and he shall not profane his word in any matter.

---

*EMET notes: Column 45 begins with the forbidden birds list (vv. 1-9), paralleling Deuteronomy 14:11-20 and Leviticus 11:13-23. The exact identification of many species is uncertain. The column then transitions to vow regulations (vv. 11-16), reworking Numbers 30:2-3 and Deuteronomy 23:21-23. The vow legislation uses first-person divine speech. "Binding obligation" renders issar (a self-imposed restriction).*
